clue.text: Poet holds straw back for the new party girl?

indicators.note: the poet's name holds, that is contains, the other piece within it

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: back tells you the word for a straw is written right to left

parts.note: a drinking straw is a thin tube

explanation.surface: A poet keeps a drinking straw in reserve for a girl who is new on the party scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the playful description of a young woman coming out into society; 'for the' merely joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: a young woman making her first appearance in society is new to its balls and dances.

clue.text: Substitute Manchester United called on laughably, heads turning

indicators.note: turning tells you the collected initial letters are written in the opposite order
heads are the tops of the words, so take the opening letter of each of the five

explanation.surface: Manchester United's manager brings on a replacement player to general derision, and the crowd look round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' takes the initials M, U, C, O, L and 'turning' writes them the other way round. The football scene hides a stand-in doctor or priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in doctor or clergyman covers for the regular one, so is a replacement.

clue.text: House of Lords style outspoken

indicators.note: outspoken, read as spoken out, tells you the word for style is said and heard as another word

parts.note: a style of doing something is a manner

explanation.surface: The upper chamber of Parliament is known for its frank way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' has MANNER said to give the answer. The capital L suggests Britain's upper chamber of Parliament, but the phrase just means a house where lords live.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the big house on an estate was the residence of the local lord.

clue.text: Journalist taken in by pulling power — that's the art of it!

indicators.note: taken in by tells you the journalist goes inside the word for pulling power

parts.note: suction is the force that pulls things in
ED is short for editor, a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter falls for someone's charm, and the clue admires the skill involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans back on the wordplay: 'pulling' is British slang for attracting a partner, and 'it' refers to that.
explanation.definitionFit: The skill of attracting and winning someone over romantically is exactly the art behind pulling.

clue.text: Condiment with Armagnac visible in a salad

indicators.note: a salad is a tossed mixture, so the letters of the two words beside it are tossed together

explanation.surface: A dressing with a noticeable splash of French brandy in a bowl of leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a salad' rearranges ARMAGNAC VISIBLE; it reads as the place the dressing is served, which is what makes it a neat signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the dark sweet Italian dressing from Modena is a seasoning added at the table.

clue.text: Cutting crime, academic sybarite

indicators.note: cutting tells you the academic cuts into the word for a crime, splitting it

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A pleasure-loving professor does his bit to reduce lawbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting crime' reads as reducing lawbreaking, but 'Cutting' means one word slicing into another.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both are people devoted to luxury and pleasure.

clue.text: European money secures cooler Irish author

indicators.note: secures tells you the currency holds the cooler inside it

parts.note: the leu is the currency of Romania
a fan cools a room

explanation.surface: Continental funding lands a more laid-back writer from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is Sheridan, the Dublin author of Victorian ghost stories such as Carmilla; 'cooler' is a thing that cools, not a comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Sheridan, the Dublin-born Victorian writer of Gothic tales, bore this surname.

clue.text: Endlessly kick around something to throw

indicators.note: endlessly tells you the phrase's synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: to kick an idea around is to discuss it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps booting about an object that is really meant to be hurled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' removes the last S of DISCUSS. 'Kick around' looks physical but means talking an idea over.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the heavy disc hurled in athletics is an object made for throwing.

clue.text: Prophet who's not all there in store for primate

indicators.note: in tells you the shortened prophet sits inside the word for a store

parts.note: a mart is a shop or market

indicators.note: not all there means the prophet's name is incomplete, here missing its last letter

parts.note: Moses is the Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A slightly unhinged seer is waiting in a shop to see an archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, and 'not all there' someone slightly mad; it is the zoological sense, and a name left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: this small South American monkey belongs to the order that includes apes and humans.

clue.text: City liberal in party has to remain suspended, for the most part

indicators.note: in tells you the word for liberal goes inside the word for a party

parts.note: a band is a group or party of people
right-on describes someone with fashionably liberal views

indicators.note: for the most part means most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to hover is to stay hanging in the air

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician must stay barred from her party for most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The two neighbouring seaside towns on England's south coast became a single city in 2000. 'Suspended' suggests a politician barred from a party; it means hanging in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the joined seaside resorts in East Sussex were granted this status in 2000.

clue.text: Maybe briefs king on a new, rude novel

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the king comes last
novel means new or different, so the three words before it take a new arrangement

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone is giving the monarch a rundown of a fresh, bawdy book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefs' looks like a verb, instructing the monarch, but it is the noun for pants.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: short close-fitting pants are one kind of garment worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: Intimate spotted scratching head

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, and the head is the first letter of the word for spotted

parts.note: a spotted or spotty face is pimply

explanation.surface: A close friend is seen puzzling over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' removes the first letter of PIMPLY. 'Intimate' reads as an adjective or a close friend, but it is the verb meaning to hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: both mean to suggest something without stating it outright.

clue.text: Device by which old magistrate implicates daughter

indicators.note: implicates is used in its old sense of entwining or folding in, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of old Venice or Genoa
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A retired judge uses some gadget to pin a crime on his own girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'implicates' puts D inside DOGE. The definition is not a gadget but a trick or ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms in the sense of a cunning trick or scheme for avoiding something.

clue.text: Hush hush reports etc, not opened, distributed

indicators.note: distributed means spread about, so the letters are dealt out in a different order
not opened means the word reports lacks its opening letter

explanation.surface: Confidential files and the like were handed round still sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opened' drops the R of REPORTS and 'distributed' rearranges EPORTS ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe information of the highest confidentiality, kept from all but a few.

clue.text: Release from duty: March the First in bed

parts.note: a protest march is a demo, short for demonstration

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter, here that of bed

explanation.surface: A soldier is let off work and spends the first of March under the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the First in' takes the B of bed. 'March the First' looks like a date, but splits: March is the protest, and 'the First' belongs with 'in bed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for demobilise, the verb for discharging troops from military service.

clue.text: Report has lied about someone from Asia

parts.note: a report is the bang of a gun or explosion

indicators.note: about means the letters of the two words before it are moved around

explanation.surface: An official account has told untruths concerning a person from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges HAS LIED into LADESHI. 'Report' looks like a document, but is a loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a native of the country on the Bay of Bengal, whose capital is Dhaka.

clue.text: Area where coach carries sovereign

indicators.note: carries tells you the word for coach holds the sovereign inside it

parts.note: to coach someone is to train them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the cipher of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A district through which a bus transports the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a vehicle; it is the verb meaning to teach.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms for a stretch of land, especially with regard to its physical features.

clue.text: Home to house wine that's most unpalatable

indicators.note: to house means the first piece gives room to the wine inside it

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone brings back the cheap plonk, the worst-tasting bottle imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House wine' reads as one phrase, but splits into the container signal and the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as superlatives: the thing most unpleasant to taste or swallow.

clue.text: Back four heading for exit, leaves

parts.note: the back of something is its end
IV is four in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the heading is the top, so take the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A football team's defence makes for the door and departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' takes the first letter of exit. A 'back four' is a football defence, and 'leaves' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for salad foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a bitter salad plant, eaten for its crisp foliage.

clue.text: Permit silence in order

indicators.note: in order means the letters of the word before it are put into a proper arrangement

explanation.surface: A judge calls the court to order and allows quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges SILENCE. The surface echoes a judge's cry of 'Silence in court!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs meaning to authorise or allow officially.

clue.text: Greek character's eastern energy

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet, the twenty-second, written like an X
the life force that flows through the body in Chinese philosophy and medicine, also spelt qi

explanation.surface: A person from Greece shows a vitality typical of the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a letter of the Hellenic alphabet, and the vital force of Chinese philosophy.

clue.text: One searching for gems, we hear, requiring case for diamonds perhaps?

indicators.note: we hear tells you the word for the gem seeker is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a miner digs for gems and minerals
a case in court is a lawsuit, or suit

explanation.surface: A prospector for precious stones needs a box to keep his diamonds in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns MINER into MINOR. In bridge, clubs and diamonds rank below hearts and spades and score less.
explanation.definitionFit: An example from bridge: clubs and this are the two lower-scoring groups of cards.

clue.text: Chirpy customer starts to get riled like someone in a supermarket?

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
a person in a supermarket is a shopper

explanation.surface: A cheerful client begins to lose their temper, as people do in the grocery aisles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes G and R. 'Customer' is informal for a creature or character, and 'chirpy' is literal: the insect chirps.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description: this jumping insect makes a chirping sound by rubbing its legs.

clue.text: Confiscating passport, that man sure is narrow-minded!

indicators.note: confiscating means taking possession of, so the pronoun takes the passport inside itself

parts.note: that man is he
a passport is a form of ID, identification
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: The official who takes away your travel papers certainly has a blinkered outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe someone rigidly conventional and unwilling to accept other ideas.

clue.text: Normal amount, a little delivery from the air

parts.note: par is the standard or expected level, as in golf or finance
a drop is a small quantity

explanation.surface: The usual quantity arrives, a small consignment sent by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies or troops let down by parachute from an aircraft arrive this way.

clue.text: Throw punch ultimately into middle of mouth and tongue

indicators.note: the middle of the word mouth is its central letter
into tells you the single letter from punch goes inside the other pieces joined together

parts.note: Norse is the old language, or tongue, of Scandinavia

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A brawler lands a blow that goes right into his opponent's open jaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the U of mouth and 'ultimately' the H of punch; 'into' puts that H inside U plus NORSE. 'Throw' looks like part of 'throw punch' but stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider thrown from the saddle has been dislodged in exactly this sense.

clue.text: Where Kipling poem's found in time of crisis?

indicators.note: found asks where the poem's title is located, and the place it sits spells the solution

parts.note: Kipling's best-known poem is If, and those two letters sit at the centre of the word life

explanation.surface: Someone seeks out a stirring verse by Kipling when everything is going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's famous poem is 'If', and those two letters are the centre of the word 'life'. 'Where ... found' asks for that location, which is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle years are proverbially when people suffer a loss of confidence and identity.

clue.text: Powerful figure boxed by dope

indicators.note: boxed by means enclosed, so the number is shut inside the word for dope

parts.note: pot and dope are both slang for cannabis
ten is a number, or figure

explanation.surface: A strong man gets hit in the ring by a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a boxing match and an idiot; 'dope' is the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe something strong and having great effect.

clue.text: Mummy's home late: seeing daddy up, discontentment ends

indicators.note: ends means the last letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: Mother gets in late, finds father still awake, and the bad mood lifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes the final letters of five words. 'Mummy' reads as mother, but is the embalmed body of a pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the land of the pharaohs is where embalmed bodies were entombed.

clue.text: Firework not seen going up? On the contrary!

indicators.note: the contrary of not seen going up is seen going up: in a down clue the word reads the same upwards as downwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A rocket nobody watched climbing into the sky, or quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the statement: the word, unlike the firework, is seen going up, reading the same upwards in the grid as downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A firework that fails to ignite and never leaves the ground is called this.
